summary: The note collects episodes from the dissolution of the Soviet Union (1985-1991), covering Gorbachev's reforms, the 1989 revolutions in Eastern Europe, nationalist and religious movements in Kazakhstan, Ukraine, Moldova and Lithuania, and the 1991 coup attempt. It concludes with the Belavezha Accords of December 1991, the lowering of the Soviet flag on December 25, and the formal end of the USSR on December 26.
one_line: Overview of the Soviet Union's collapse, from Gorbachev's reforms and national movements to the Belavezha Accords and the USSR's end in December 1991.
key_facts: In spring 1989 Soviet citizens elected the Congress of People's Deputies in their first limited democratic choice since 1917, with uncensored live TV coverage of its debates.
Gorbachev abandoned the Brezhnev Doctrine in favor of non-intervention in allies' affairs, jokingly called the Sinatra Doctrine after Frank Sinatra's song "My Way".
The 1989 revolutions peacefully toppled Soviet-imposed communist regimes in the Warsaw Pact, with Romania excepted.
The Jeltoqsan riots began December 17, 1986 in Alma-Ata after Gorbachev replaced Kazakh Dinmukhamed Konayev with Russian outsider Gennady Kolbin.
On December 7, 1989 the Communist Party of Lithuania under Algirdas Brazauskas split from the CPSU, a first for Soviet republics.
Vytautas Landsbergis became the first non-Communist president of Lithuania since its incorporation into the USSR after multiparty elections in 1990.
In May 1985 Gorbachev launched an anti-alcohol campaign that cut annual alcohol tax collections by 100 billion rubles, according to Alexander Yakovlev.
A New Union Treaty to turn the USSR into a federation was to be signed by the Russian SFSR on August 20, 1991, and was strongly supported by the Central Asian republics.
During the 1991 coup, Yeltsin rallied resistance atop a tank at the White House; the plotters failed to arrest him or jam foreign broadcasts like CNN and BBC World Service.
On December 8, 1991 the leaders of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus signed the Belavezha Accords in Belavezhskaya Pushcha, declaring the USSR ended and founding the Commonwealth of Independent States.
On December 12, 1991 the Russian SFSR Supreme Soviet ratified the Accords and recalled its deputies, leaving the Union's Council of the Union without a quorum.
The Soviet flag was lowered for the last time at 7:32 p.m. Moscow time on December 25, 1991, and the Council of Republics dissolved the USSR on December 26, 1991.
On June 4, 1990 Volodymyr Ivashko was elected chair of the Ukrainian parliament with 60 percent of the vote as over 100 opposition deputies boycotted.
The Ukrainian Autocephalous Orthodox Church elected Metropolitan Mstyslav patriarch on June 5-6, 1990, and enthroned him at Saint Sophia's Cathedral on November 18, 1990.
